newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Options speculators push Israeli shares up.
newsitem.headline: Options speculators push Israeli shares up.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed up across the board on Wednesday in very thin trading with most of the activity from options speculators, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.24 percent, or 2.28 points, to 186.33 on turnover of 47 million shekels against 56 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.34 percent to 196.91.
"Activity continues to be very low and the only active players are Maof (options) speculators. The market's rise is nothing but a technical correction," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
Dead Sea Bromine surged 5.75 percent to 1569. Traders noted that the share rose on volume of less than 240,000 shekels.

Agan Chemical Manufacturers gained 1.25 percent to 5,139 after Bank Hapoalim issued a buy recommendation for the share saying it is greatly undervalued. The bank said the company was valued at $300 million to $320 million against its present market valuation of $244 million.
"With such low activity today's rise is meaningless. The rise might be an outcome of high activity of options speculators," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The shekel's decline also had some impact on shares of Israeli exporters," he said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2670 shekels against 3.2560 on Tuesday.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 1.25 percent to 130,076 on volume of 3.4 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.75 percent to 448 on turnover of 3.1 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which rose 0.25 percent to 28,181 on volume of 2.3 million shekels.
